case_title: DATTATRAYA @ DATTA AMBO ROKADE v. THE STATE OF MAHARASHTRA
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.376(2)(f), s.377, s.363, s.364, s.367 and 201 r/w ss. 3,4,5 (i) (l) and (m) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
confession: Extra-judicial confession made by the accused to his wife, relied on
aggravating_circumstances: Rape and murder of a minor child
neutral_facts: The accused, a 53-year-old man, was convicted of raping and murdering a 5-year-old girl. The victim was found dead in the accused's tenement, with severe injuries consistent with sexual assault and asphyxia. Forensic evidence, including DNA analysis, linked the accused to the crime. The accused confessed to his wife, who was a witness. The trial court imposed a death sentence, but the Supreme Court commuted it to life imprisonment, citing inadequate consideration of mitigating circumstances and procedural deficiencies in the sentencing process.
